sources.title: Publication 550, Investment Income and Expenses
sources.scope: DRIP taxation, holding period, discounted DRIP basis
sources.verification_note: Quoted: dividends used to buy more stock must still be reported as income; holding period of each reinvested share begins the day after purchase; discounted DRIP basis is full FMV on the payment date.

sources.title: Topic 703, Basis of Assets
sources.verification_note: Quoted: basis of purchased stocks or bonds is the purchase price plus additional costs such as commissions.

sources.title: Topic 404, Dividends
sources.verification_note: General page on dividend taxation; HTTP 200 on 2026-10-26.

statistics.claim: 100 shares at $50 with a $0.50 quarterly dividend, reinvested for five years with no growth, reach about 122.019 shares worth about $6,100.95; annual dividend income about $244.04.
statistics.method: Fin Loom calculation, period by period (100 x 1.01^20)

evidence_map: Publication 550: reinvested dividends reportable as income; holding period per reinvested share; discounted DRIP basis (quoted).
Topic 703: basis is purchase price plus costs (quoted).

claims.statement: Dividends used to buy more stock must still be reported as income.
The holding period of each reinvested share begins the day after that share was purchased.
Basis of purchased stock is the purchase price plus additional costs such as commissions.
